title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a local, check things with tag questions, add emphasis with Odia's little particles, use echo words and word pairs, ask people to repeat or explain, and mix in English the way young Odias do.
intro:
You can now say almost anything you need — this unit is about saying it the way people actually talk. Real conversation is full of small words that carry the attitude: **ସତ କହୁଛ?** 'seriously?', **ଧେତ୍!** 'come off it!', **ଏକଦମ୍!** 'exactly!', a **ନା?** on the end to check you agree, a **ସିନା** to say 'OK, granted, but…', a **ରେ** after a friend's name.

You'll also learn Odia's habit of saying things twice — echo words like **ଚା-ଫା** 'tea and stuff', pairs like **ଲୁଗାପଟା** 'clothes and all' and doubles like **ଗରମ ଗରମ** 'piping hot' — and the survival lines for when you don't catch something or don't know a word. Finally, the English: every young Odia mixes it in (ଆକ୍ଚୁଆଲି, ଆଡଜଷ୍ଟ, ମ୍ୟାନେଜ୍), and so can you — as long as you know when to switch it off.

vocab.en: come off it!, get away!, nonsense! (familiar)
vocab.note: Playful dismissal between friends. Not for elders.
Said with a closed mouth to show you're following, or while thinking.
Used everywhere, also as a tag: କାଲି ଆସିବୁ, ଓକେ?
Among friends; with strangers and elders ଦୟାକରି or a polite verb is better.
Concedes one point to contrast it with another: ମୁଁ ସିନା ଡେରି କଲି, ତୁ ତ ଆସିଲୁ ହିଁ ନାହିଁ!

vocab.en: (calling particle) hey (to a friend or younger person)
vocab.note: After a name or at the end: ରବି ରେ! · ହଁ ରେ. Intimate — never with ଆପଣ-people.

vocab.en: (calling particle) hey (to a girl or woman you're close to)
vocab.note: ଅପା ଲୋ! · ମା ଲୋ! (also an exclamation: 'oh mother!'). Intimate.
Fused ସେ + ହିଁ. Likewise ଏଇ 'this very'.

vocab.en: tea and snacks, tea or something (echo word)
vocab.note: The echo -ଫା means 'and that kind of thing'.
Lit. 'whatever it be' — the classic way to change the subject.
In speech also ମାନେ: ଏହାର ମାନେ କ'ଣ?
Hugely common filler in young people's Odia. Odia equivalent: ପ୍ରକୃତରେ.
ଆଡଜଷ୍ଟ କରିବା = to make do, to make room — very Indian English.
ମ୍ୟାନେଜ୍ କରିବା = to manage, cope; ମ୍ୟାନେଜ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ = it'll work out.

phrases.note: Lit. 'are you telling the truth?'. To a ତୁ-friend: ସତ କହୁଛୁ?

phrases.en: Come on, let's have some tea or something.
What did you say? I didn't catch that.
That thing… what do you call it?

grammar.title: Tag questions: …, ନା? and friends
grammar.body:
English tags change with the verb ('isn't it?', 'won't you?', 'did she?'). Odia tags never change — pick one and put it on the end, after a little pause:

**…, ନା?** — the all-purpose 'right?', for any tense, positive or negative: ତୁମେ ଆସିବ, ନା? 'you're coming, right?'; ସେ କାଲି ଆସିଥିଲା, ନା? 'she came yesterday, didn't she?'
**…, ନୁହେଁ କି?** — 'isn't it / aren't you?', a little more careful: ଏହା ସତ, ନୁହେଁ କି?
**…, ଠିକ୍ ତ?** — 'right?' to check a fact or plan: ସାତଟାରେ, ଠିକ୍ ତ?
**… ତ?** — hoping for 'yes' (unit 20): ସବୁ ଭଲ ତ?
**…, ହଁ? / …, ଓକେ?** — after an instruction: 'OK?': ଲେଟ୍ କରିବୁ ନାହିଁ, ହଁ?
**…, ନା କ'ଣ?** — 'or what?', impatient or teasing: ତୁ ଆସୁଛୁ ନା କ'ଣ?

**Answering** a negative question ('aren't you coming?') is confusing in every language, and Odia ହଁ / ନା can mean 'yes, you're right (I'm not)'. The natural, safe answer repeats the verb: ତୁମେ ଚା ପିଇବ ନାହିଁ? — **ପିଇବି**, ଟିକେ ପରେ 'I will, a bit later' / **ନା, ପିଇବି ନାହିଁ** 'no, I won't'.

The trap: a tag needs the comma-pause and rising tone. Said flat and run on, **…ନା** can sound like 'or' (ଚା ନା କଫି? 'tea or coffee?').

examples.en: We're watching the match tomorrow, right?

examples.native: ତୁ ଯିବୁ ନାହିଁ? — ଯିବି, ଟିକେ ପରେ।
examples.roman: tu jibu nahiṃ? — jibi, ṭike pôre.
examples.en: Aren't you going? — I am, a bit later.

grammar.title: Emphasis and attitude: ସିନା, ତ, ହିଁ, ଏକଦମ୍, ରେ / ଲୋ
grammar.body:
Unit 20 introduced **ତ**, **ହିଁ** and **ବି**. A few more tiny words do a lot of work in real conversation. They all sit **right after the word they colour**.

**ସିନା** — 'granted, X…, but': it concedes one point to set up a contrast. Very Odia, and constant in friendly arguments: ମୁଁ **ସିନା** ଡେରିରେ ଆସିଲି, ତୁ ତ ଆସିଲୁ ହିଁ ନାହିଁ! 'OK, *I* came late — but you didn't come at all!'; ସେ ସିନା ଧନୀ, କିନ୍ତୁ… 'sure, he's rich, but…'.

**ତ vs ହିଁ**: **ତ** adds attitude — 'well, after all, I *did*': ମୁଁ ତ କହିଥିଲି 'I *did* tell you'. **ହିଁ** pins down exactly which — 'the very one, no one else': ମୁଁ ହିଁ କହିଥିଲି 'it was *me* who told you'. Fused forms: ସେ + ହିଁ → **ସେଇ** 'that very', ଏ + ହିଁ → **ଏଇ**.

**ଏକଦମ୍** 'totally, absolutely' — a reaction (ଏକଦମ୍! 'exactly!') and an intensifier (ଏକଦମ୍ ଠିକ୍, ଏକଦମ୍ ନୂଆ). Its negative partner is **ଜମା** '(not) at all' from unit 20.

**Doubling** a word intensifies or spreads it: ଗରମ ଗରମ ଚା 'piping-hot tea', ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ 'slowly, little by little', ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ପିଲା 'little kids'.

**Calling particles** after a name or at the end of a line: **ରେ** to a friend or someone younger (ରବି ରେ! · ହଁ ରେ), **ଲୋ** to a girl or woman you're close to (ଅପା ଲୋ!). Both are intimate — never with someone you call ଆପଣ.

The trap: move the particle and you move the stress. ମୁଁ ସିନା ଡେରିରେ ଆସିଲି stresses *I*; ମୁଁ ଡେରିରେ ସିନା ଆସିଲି stresses *late* ('I came late, sure, but I came').

examples.native: ମୁଁ ସିନା ଡେରିରେ ଆସିଲି, ତୁ ତ ଆସିଲୁ ହିଁ ନାହିଁ!
examples.roman: muṃ sina ḍerire asili, tu tô asilu hiṃ nahiṃ!
examples.en: OK, I came late — but you didn't come at all!
It was me who told you.

grammar.title: Echo words and word pairs
grammar.body:
Odia loves saying things twice. Three patterns:

**1. Echo words** — repeat a word with its first sound replaced, usually by **ଫ-**: **ଚା-ଫା** 'tea and stuff', ବହି-ଫହି 'books and so on'. The echo means 'X and that sort of thing' and makes an offer or question sound easy-going: ଚା-ଫା ହେବ? 'tea or something?'. Some speakers echo with ଟ- instead. Keep echo words for relaxed talk — not in an email to your boss.

**2. Fixed pairs** — two related words that together mean 'X and all that': ଜିନିଷପତ୍ର 'stuff' (unit 35), **ଲୁଗାପଟା** 'clothes', **ଟଙ୍କାପଇସା** 'money', **କାମଧନ୍ଦା** 'work, business', **ଘରଦ୍ୱାର** 'house and home', **ପାଣିପାଗ** 'weather, climate', ଦେଖାଶୁଣା 'looking after' (unit 26). These are ordinary words, fine in polite speech.

**3. Doubled words** — the same word twice for 'each / all the various', or for something repeated or ongoing: କିଏ କିଏ ଆସିଥିଲେ? 'who (all) came?', କ'ଣ କ'ଣ କିଣିଲ? 'what (all) did you buy?', ଗାଧୋଇ ଗାଧୋଇ 'bathing again and again' (unit 35), ବସି ବସି 'sitting around'.

The trap: an echo word is always vague. ଚା-ଫା can't mean one particular cup — for that, just say ଗୋଟିଏ ଚା.

examples.en: Have you packed all your clothes and stuff?
Who all came to the party?

dialogue.title: What does ସିନା mean?
dialogue.setting: A tea stall near Ravenshaw College, Cuttack. Sam, who has been learning Odia for a year, meets his friend Rabi.

lines.speaker: Rabi
lines.native: ବାପରେ, ତୁ ତ ପୂରା ଓଡ଼ିଆ ହୋଇଗଲୁଣି!
lines.roman: bapôre, tu tô pura Oṛia hoigôluṇi!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, ଆକ୍ଚୁଆଲି ମୁଁ ଏବେ ଗୋଟେ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ସିରିଜ୍ ଦେଖୁଛି। ହେଲେ ଗୋଟେ କଥା… ସିନା ମାନେ କ'ଣ?
lines.roman: hôṃ, akchuali muṃ ebe goṭe Oṛia sirij dekhuchhi. hele goṭe kôtha… sina mane kôṇô?
lines.en: Yeah — actually I'm watching an Odia series at the moment. But one thing… what does "sina" mean?

lines.speaker: Rabi
lines.native: ଉଁ… କେମିତି ବୁଝାଇବି… ମୁଁ ସିନା ଗରିବ, ମୋ ମନ ତ ଧନୀ!
lines.roman: uṃ… kemiti bujhaibi… muṃ sina gôribô, mo mônô tô dhôni!
lines.en: Hmm… how do I explain… "Sure, I'm poor — but my heart is rich!"

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହା ହା! ମାନେ "ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ…", ନା?
lines.roman: ha ha! mane "ṭhik ôchhi, kintu…", na?
lines.en: Ha ha! So it's like "OK, but…", right?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଧେତ୍! ମୁଁ ଏବେ ବି ଅଧା କଥା ବୁଝେନି। ତୁମେମାନେ ଏତେ ଶୀଘ୍ର ଶୀଘ୍ର କଥା ହୁଅ!
lines.roman: dhet! muṃ ebe bi ôdha kôtha bujheni. tumemane ete sighrô sighrô kôtha huô!
lines.en: Come off it! I still don't get half of what's said. You lot talk so fast!

lines.speaker: Rabi
lines.native: ସେଥିପାଇଁ ତ କହୁଛି — "ଟିକେ ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ କୁହ" ବୋଲି କହିବୁ। କେହି ରାଗିବେ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: sethipaiṃ tô kôhuchhi — "ṭike dhire dhire kuhô" boli kôhibu. kehi ragibe nahiṃ.
lines.en: That's exactly why I'm telling you — just say "speak a bit slower". Nobody'll mind.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: And if I don't know a word?

lines.speaker: Rabi
lines.native: ବୁଝାଇଦେ — "ସେ ଜିନିଷଟା, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ ଚା ଛାଣନ୍ତି…"। ଇଂରାଜୀ ମିଶାଇ କହିଲେ ବି ଚଳିବ। ସମସ୍ତେ ତ ସେମିତି କରନ୍ତି, ନା?
lines.roman: bujhaide — "se jinisôṭa, jeuṃthire cha chhaṇônti…". Iṅraji misai kôhile bi chôḷibô. sômôste tô semiti kôrônti, na?
lines.en: Describe it — "that thing you strain tea with…". Mixing in English is fine too. Everyone does it anyway, right?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଓକେ, ଡନ୍। ଯାହାହେଉ, ଚା ଥଣ୍ଡା ହୋଇଗଲାଣି। ଭାଇ, ଆଉ ଦୁଇଟା ଗରମ ଗରମ ଚା!
lines.roman: oke, ḍôn. jahaheu, cha thôṇḍa hoigôlaṇi. bhai, au duiṭa gôrômô gôrômô cha!
lines.en: OK, done. Anyway, the tea's gone cold. Bhai, two more piping-hot teas!

culture:
Listen to young people in Bhubaneswar or Cuttack and you'll hear a fluid mix of Odia, English and a sprinkle of Hindi in the same sentence: ଆକ୍ଚୁଆଲି ମୁଁ ଟିକେ ବିଜି ଅଛି, ଲେଟ୍ ହେବ, ଆଡଜଷ୍ଟ କରିନେବୁ ନା? That's normal and nobody will think worse of you for doing it; in fact a foreigner who drops in **ଏକଦମ୍**, **ଧେତ୍** and **ସିନା** in the right places gets a delighted laugh. What matters is register: with grandparents, officials or at a temple, use fuller Odia, **ଆପଣ**, **ଆଜ୍ଞା**, and fewer English words — some older people take pride in 'pure' Odia (ଶୁଦ୍ଧ ଓଡ଼ିଆ) and will happily teach you the native word.

Odia sounds different around the state. Cuttack–Puri speech is the standard you've learned; in western Odisha people speak **Sambalpuri** (Kosli), with different verb endings and words — you'll hear it in hit songs; in the south (Berhampur/Ganjam) the accent and some words change again. Nobody expects you to master them, but asking 'ଏହାର ମାନେ କ'ଣ?' wins friends everywhere.

Two listening tips: Odias nod and say **ହଁ**, **ଉଁ** or **ଆଚ୍ଛା** constantly to show they're following — do the same, or you'll seem cold. And the famous Indian head-wobble means 'yes / OK / I'm with you' far more often than 'no'.

tip.title: Reactions keep the chat going
tip.body:
- Surprise: **ସତ କହୁଛ?** 'seriously?' · **ମଜା କରୁଛ କି?** 'kidding?' · **ଅସମ୍ଭବ!** 'no way!'
- Agreement: **ଏକଦମ୍!** 'exactly!'
- Friendly dismissal: **ଧେତ୍!** 'come off it!' (friends only)
- Listening noises: **ଉଁ**, **ହଁ**, ଆଚ୍ଛା — use them a lot.

sentences.native: ଅସମ୍ଭବ! ଓଡ଼ିଶା ଏ ମ୍ୟାଚ୍ ହାରିବ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: ôsômbhôbô! Oṛisa e myach haribô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: No way! Odisha won't lose this match.

sentences.roman: uṃ… hôṃ… tapôre?

sentences.roman: ehi jamaṭa ekdôm nua.
sentences.en: This shirt is brand new.

sentences.roman: bapôre! tu sôtôre sara rati pôṛhilu?
sentences.en: Wow! You really studied all night?

tip.title: …, ନା? — right?
tip.body:
- Add a tag after a pause: **ନା?** 'right?' · **ନୁହେଁ କି?** 'isn't it?' · **ଠିକ୍ ତ?** · **ହଁ? / ଓକେ?** after an instruction.
- Tags never change with the verb or tense.
- Answer with the verb: ପିଇବ ନାହିଁ? — **ପିଇବି** / **ପିଇବି ନାହିଁ**.
tip.pattern: statement, + ନା? / ନୁହେଁ କି? / ଠିକ୍ ତ?

sentences.native: ତୁ କାଲି ଅଫିସ୍ ଯିବୁ, ନା?
sentences.roman: tu kali ôphis jibu, na?
sentences.en: You're going to the office tomorrow, right?

sentences.en: This song's really good, isn't it?

sentences.native: ତୁ ଆସୁଛୁ ନା କ'ଣ? ସମସ୍ତେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: tu asuchhu na kôṇô? sômôste ôpekhya kôruchhônti.

sentences.native: ପ୍ଲିଜ୍, ଟିକେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିଦେ, ହଁ?
sentences.roman: pliz, ṭike sahajjyô kôride, hôṃ?
sentences.en: Please help me out a bit, yeah?

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଚା ପିଇବ ନାହିଁ? — ପିଇବି, ଟିକେ ପରେ।
sentences.roman: tume cha piibô nahiṃ? — piibi, ṭike pôre.
sentences.en: Aren't you having tea? — I will, a bit later.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ଆସିବ, ନା? ମୁଁ ତୁମ ପାଇଁ ଜାଗା ରଖିବି।
sentences.roman: tume asibô, na? muṃ tumô paiṃ jaga rôkhibi.
sentences.en: You're coming, right? I'll save you a seat.

tip.title: ସିନା, ତ, ହିଁ — attitude in one word
tip.body:
- **ସିନା**: 'granted X…, but' — ମୁଁ **ସିନା** ଭୁଲ କଲି, ତୁ ତ…
- **ତ**: 'I *did*, after all'; **ହିଁ**: 'it was *me*, the very one' (fused: **ସେଇ, ଏଇ**).
- Doubling: **ଗରମ ଗରମ**, **ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ**.
- Calling a friend: ରବି **ରେ**; a close girl/woman: ଅପା **ଲୋ**.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ସିନା ଭୁଲ କଲି, ତୁ ତ କିଛି କହିଲୁ ନାହିଁ!
sentences.roman: muṃ sina bhulô kôli, tu tô kichhi kôhilu nahiṃ!

sentences.native: ସେଇ ଦୋକାନରେ ମୁଁ ଫୋନ କିଣିଥିଲି।

sentences.native: ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ ମୋର ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଭଲ ହେଉଛି।
sentences.roman: dhire dhire morô Oṛia bhôlô heuchhi.
sentences.en: Little by little my Odia's getting better.

sentences.native: ସେ ସିନା ଧନୀ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଗୋଟେ ଚା ବି ପିଆଏ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: se sina dhôni, kintu goṭe cha bi piae nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Sure he's rich, but he won't even buy you a tea.

tip.title: Saying it twice
tip.body:
- Echo with **ଫ-** = 'and stuff': **ଚା-ଫା** 'tea or something'.
- Pairs = 'X and all that': **ଲୁଗାପଟା, ଟଙ୍କାପଇସା, କାମଧନ୍ଦା, ଘରଦ୍ୱାର, ପାଣିପାଗ**.
- Doubles = 'all the various': **କିଏ କିଏ**, **ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ**.
- Change the subject: **ଯାହାହେଉ** 'anyway'.

sentences.native: ଆସ ଆସ, ଚା-ଫା କିଛି ନେବ?

sentences.en: Come in, come in — will you have some tea or something?

sentences.native: କାମଧନ୍ଦା ଛାଡ଼ି ସେ ସାରା ଦିନ ଫୋନ ଦେଖୁଛି।

sentences.en: I like the weather here.

sentences.native: ଘରଦ୍ୱାର ଛାଡ଼ି ବିଦେଶରେ ରହିବା ସହଜ ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: ghôrôdwarô chhaṛi bidesôre rôhiba sôhôjô nuheṃ.
sentences.en: It isn't easy to leave home behind and live abroad.

sentences.native: ଯାହାହେଉ, ତୁମେ କେମିତି ଅଛ?

sentences.native: ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ପିଲାମାନେ ବାହାରେ ଖେଳୁଛନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: chhoṭô chhoṭô pilamane bahare kheḷuchhônti.
sentences.en: Little kids are playing outside.

tip.title: Repeat, slow down, explain
tip.body:
- Didn't hear: **କ'ଣ କହିଲ? ଶୁଭିଲା ନାହିଁ।** (polite: ଦୋହରାଇବେ କି?)
- Too fast: **ଟିକେ ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ କୁହ / କୁହନ୍ତୁ**.
- A word: **… ର ଅର୍ଥ କ'ଣ?** or **… ମାନେ କ'ଣ?**
- Don't know the word? Describe it: **ସେ ଜିନିଷଟା, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ …**

sentences.native: ମାଫ କରିବେ, ଆଉ ଥରେ ଦୋହରାଇବେ କି?

sentences.en: Sorry, could you repeat that once more?

sentences.native: ଦୟାକରି ଟିକେ ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ କୁହନ୍ତୁ, ମୁଁ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଶିଖୁଛି।

sentences.native: ସେ ଜିନିଷଟା, ଯେଉଁଥିରେ ଭାତ ରାନ୍ଧନ୍ତି… ଓଡ଼ିଆରେ କ'ଣ କହନ୍ତି?

sentences.en: I remember a word by repeating it over and over.

tip.title: English + Odia verbs
tip.body:
- English nouns and adjectives take Odia verbs: **ଆଡଜଷ୍ଟ କରିବା**, **ମ୍ୟାନେଜ୍ କରିବା**, ମ୍ୟାନେଜ୍ **ହୋଇଯିବ**.
- Fillers: **ଆକ୍ଚୁଆଲି**, **ଓକେ**, **ସରି**, **ପ୍ଲିଜ୍**.
- With elders and officials: less English, more ଆପଣ and ଆଜ୍ଞା.

sentences.native: ଆକ୍ଚୁଆଲି ମୁଁ ଆଜି ଟିକେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ଅଛି।

sentences.native: ଛୋଟ ଫ୍ଲାଟ୍, କିନ୍ତୁ ଆଡଜଷ୍ଟ କରିନେବା।

sentences.native: ଜେଜେମାଙ୍କ ସହ କଥା ହେବା ବେଳେ ବେଶି ଇଂରାଜୀ ମିଶାଅ ନାହିଁ।
